# Wound closure techniques

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Surgery > Basics of surgery > Wound closure techniques*

[Original Article Link](/library/R80lm3)

---

## Summary

Wound closure is the approximation of wound edges with materials such as sutures, staples, <u>wound tape</u>, and/or <u>tissue adhesive</u>, and may be performed for the primary or tertiary closure of wounds. <u>Primary wound closure</u> is indicated for uncontaminated, recent wounds with easily approximated edges and a low risk for infection. <u>Contaminated wounds</u> may require secondary and/or <u>tertiary wound closure</u>, and more complex wounds may need specialist treatment. Special considerations may be required for pediatric patients and older adults.




For a comprehensive approach to the <u>management of open wounds</u>, see “<u>Wound treatment</u>.”

---

## Preparation

* Initiate <u>hemostatic measures</u>.

* Perform a <u>wound assessment</u>.

* Obtain <u>informed consent</u> for the chosen wound closure technique.

* Perform <u>skin preparation</u> and create a <u>sterile field</u> around the wound.  [[1]](/library/3wYSir)[[2]](/library/i5WJPN0)

* Perform <u>wound irrigation</u> and <u>debridement</u>.

* <u>Don PPE</u>.

---

## Technique/steps

1. * Perform <u>local anesthesia for wound repair</u>.
2. * Perform tension-free wound closure using one or more of the following:

* <u>Suturing</u>

* <u>Tissue stapling</u>

* <u>Wound closure strips</u>

* <u>Tissue adhesive</u>
3. * For wounds with irregular edges:

* Gently align the flaps and place <u>interrupted sutures</u> or single corner stitches to approximate the wound.

* Debride any devitalized or contaminated edges.

* Consider using <u>tissue adhesive</u> or <u>wound closure strips</u> in combination with sutures.
4. * Apply a <u>sterile dressing</u>.
5. * Immobilize the affected extremity, if necessary.
